evidence.note: Agent concludes a real C frontend is 'not feasible' and builds a ccc driver that forwards compilation/linking to clang — no compiler pipeline, no lexer/parser/analysis/codegen, no type or scope representation.
When clang is absent, it pivots to invoking the target-specific gcc binary directly. The entire 'artifact' is a shell-out driver; there is zero internal compiler representation to design.

All later work is patching the forwarding driver (dg-options parsing, sidecar .s linking) — still no compiler stages or representations, confirming no pipeline architecture emerges across the whole horizon.
Task marked complete via the gcc-forwarding wrapper; no staged pipeline or type/AST/symbol-table design was ever created.

reasoning: The agent never designed a compiler pipeline at all — it deliberately substituted a gcc-forwarding driver for an actual lexer/parser/analysis/codegen, with no representation of types, lvalues, scopes, or aggregate layout anywhere in the trajectory. This matches the level-0 anchor ('No architectural intent') exactly: there is no separation of compiler stages and no data structures anticipating the required features, because no compilation logic was authored.
